newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: HIGH OIL PRICES SEEN NUDGING S.AFRICA INFLATION UP.
newsitem.headline: HIGH OIL PRICES SEEN NUDGING S.AFRICA INFLATION UP.

text.p: High world oil prices are expected to fuel a five percent rise in local gasoline prices over the next two months, but the impact on producer and consumer inflation will be muted, economists said on Monday.

World benchmark Brent Blend oil has risen $7 a barrel since June amid concerns about renewed tensions in the Middle East and on the back of persistently low stocks of heating oil in the U.S. and Europe.
South Africa imports some 400,000 barrels of oil a day.

Transnet economist Mike Schussler estimates that as a result of higher international oil prices, local gasoline prices -- currently set at 210 cents a litre -- will rise by three cents in November and then by a further six cents in December.

SMK Securities economist Herman van Papendorp said a 10 to 15 cent increase in the fuel price over the next two months would contribute about 0.2 percent to the monthly increase in consumer inflation, running at 7.5 percent year-on-year in August.
"Obviously it is negative but is not that pronounced because it only has 3.1 percent weighting in the overall (consumer price) index," he said.
Producer inflation is also expected to be prodded higher, particularly as the price of diesel -- generally used by producers -- is also rising.

Schussler said that he expected the diesel price to rise to 211 cents in November from the current 204 cents. By December he said the price of diesel will have risen to 215 cents per litre, 26 percent higher than a year ago.
Producer inflation could also be lifted by the same 0.2 percent margin as CPI as a result of the higher petrol and diesel prices, economists said. PPI in August rose 7.4 percent year-year.
However, van Papendorp also noted that while oil prices had been rising, producer inflation data thus far had yet to reflect the 20 percent rise in rand oil prices since May this year.

Oil price movements are reflected in the "other minerals" category in the producer price index. The category has a 4.33 percent weighting in the overall index, nearly half of which is accounted for by liquid petroleum.
After a 3.5 percent month-on-month rise in June, the category slowed to a 0.1 percent rise in July and decreased by 0.6 percent in August.
Van Papendorp said that from May to the end of September, the rand oil price had risen from 78.31 to 105.10 per barrel.
"I am a little bit worried about the PPI...I think we are not catching all the price increases in the statistics," he said.
"I am worried that we might see a bump somewhere along the line...and that it could come through in a big bulk in one month," van Papendorp said.
If this did prove to be the case, he said producer inflation could peak at around 9.5 percent at year-end, compared to initial hopes of an 8.5 percent peak, he said.
